topic: Theorems of Perpendicular and Parallel Axes
title: Three Spins? Axes Theorems Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A gate swings about its hinge, a wheel turns on its axle, a pendulum swings from near its top. And Diya spins one coin three ways: flat, on its edge, and on a pin through its rim. Three different moments of inertia. Must she work out each from scratch? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the two shortcuts: the theorems of perpendicular and parallel axes.

Syllabus note: these two theorems are not in the current (rationalised) NCERT book. They are in the ISC (CISCE) Class 11 syllabus and in the JEE Main and NEET syllabus.

We build the perpendicular axes theorem link by link for a flat coin, then on a live motion notebook move the axis of a spinning disc out from its centre, while the readout tracks d, Md squared and I, and a graph shows I against d squared as a straight line that starts at Icm with the mass as its slope. A slow-mo replay splits the motion into the centre going round and the spin about the centre. We show step by step why I = Icm + Md squared, compare a rod about its middle and its end, and find I of a disc about a tangent using both theorems. Then the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
